summary: All 67 functions in net_chunk_002.c belong to Tencent's TDR/TLV packet codec (source files TdrBuf.h + TdrBufUtil.cpp), NOT stock CryEngine transport. They are per-struct (de)serializers and text-dump (DebugFormat) helpers for game-protocol structures used by CryGame.dll. There are no message dispatchers, RMI stubs, channel or session objects in this chunk, and no opcode/msgId is resolvable (these are struct-level codecs invoked by higher-level message handlers). Each concrete struct appears as an A/B pair plus an optional PRINT function: variant A uses helpers FUN_1010c560/FUN_1010c680/FUN_1010cbd0 and emits wire-type 0 (VARINT) tags; variant B uses FUN_1010c190/FUN_1010c200/FUN_1010c870 and emits wire-type 3 (4-byte)/4 (8-byte) fixed tags. Variant B matches the tag encoding in the generated TLV docs, so B is the canonical wire form; A is a varint-compact alternate. Read helpers: FUN_1010ccb0=read tag/varint, FUN_1010c870=read len-prefixed size, FUN_1010cbd0=read zigzag varint, FUN_1010d4f0=skip unknown field. Write helpers: FUN_1010c5f0=write 1 byte(tag/uint8), FUN_1010c0c0=write uint8 field, FUN_1010c2b0=write string bytes, FUN_1010bf70=reserve 4-byte length placeholder, FUN_1010c3c0=backfill length prefix. Server relevance: HIGH for every struct here — a private server must implement byte-identical TDR (de)serialization for these to exchange player data (settings, friends, cat-cuisine, weapon records, action points, channel tabs) with the retail client.
